source_title: Delivering Cognitive Behavior Therapy to Young Adults With Symptoms of Depression and Anxiety Using a Fully Automated Conversational Agent (Woebot): A Randomized Controlled Trial

notes: Small sample, short duration, non-clinical population (self-identified symptoms, not diagnosed), and co-authorship by a Woebot Labs employee are relevant limitations to interpretation

source_title: Efficacy and Conflicts of Interest in Randomized Controlled Trials Evaluating Headspace and Calm Apps: Systematic Review
finding_detail: Peer-reviewed systematic review identified 14 RCTs of Headspace; found depression improved in 75% of studies measuring it, mixed/partial findings for anxiety, stress, and wellbeing, most studies underpowered, and 50% of RCTs disclosed a conflict of interest involving Headspace (e.g., free premium access, in 2 cases employee involvement in study design)
claim_text_or_summary: Systematic review reports Headspace improved depression outcomes in a majority of RCTs examined, with mixed results for other outcomes and notable conflict-of-interest patterns
notes: This is a review of RCTs, not a single trial; conflict-of-interest and underpowering issues identified by the review authors should be preserved alongside any effectiveness claim
